harvest.verdict_reason: Wave 2 added 86 MUST rules and new agent failure classes in 7 freshly opened families. 8 of 15 ID families (SW-LANG, API, NET, SEC, REL, APPLE, CORE, BZL-SWIFT) and all 3 skills have no consolidation. Two cross-consolidation contradictions (ExplicitSendable gate form; StrictLanguageFeatures manifest form vs SW-GATE-14) leave checks unmeasured in the form the drafters would copy. Load-bearing answerable-now questions remain: TSan suppression now that seccomp is fixed; the SwiftLint SourceKit image as a carrier; test-environment isolation; SDK cancellation.

next_wave.label: Revision: bounded streams, accept-loop caps, cleanup under cancellation with the 6.4 shield and async defer
next_wave.brief:

Fetch:

- https://github.com/apple/swift-async-algorithms (AsyncChannel, AsyncThrowingChannel, multi-producer channel status)
- the AsyncStream.Continuation.BufferingPolicy docs.
Pin: AsyncStream buffering policies on 6.4; whether swift-async-algorithms is acceptable under the SDK dependency budget (owner Q4: stdlib plus swift-subprocess; expect not for the SDK, possibly for servers).
Plant in fixtures/backpressure-and-cleanup/:
(a) A fast producer into an unbounded AsyncStream against a slow consumer. Measure peak RSS via /usr/bin/time -v or /proc/self/status VmHWM. Red = unbounded growth; green = `.bufferingNewest(n)` and an AsyncChannel twin. Record the API cost of each.
(b) An accept loop that spawns a child task per connection. Measure peak in-flight tasks unbounded, against a `group.next()` window of N and a counter cap.
(c) Cleanup on cancel. The first Ctrl-C cancels the work; cleanup (a temp file unlink plus a flush) must finish before the process exits. Compare a plain `defer`, an async `defer` (6.4) and `withTaskCancellationShield` (6.4), each with a cancellable `Task.sleep` inside the cleanup. Red = cleanup skipped or cut short; green = it completes. Feeds SW-CLI-11 and cli/services-and-config.
(d) Confirm the 6.3 diagnostics for (c) so libraries at the 6.2 floor know what to use (`#if compiler(>=6.4)`).
Decide:
- The bounded-stream rule and the default buffering policy.
- The accept-loop cap rule for servers.
- The cleanup-under-cancellation rule and its floor.
- Whether AsyncChannel is recommended, and for which code kinds.

(b) One binary with a subcommand per failure: precondition, force unwrap, a segfault in a C call, SIGPIPE, a continuation leak (hang, 124 under timeout), a data race (TSan) and a slow type-check. Each runbook step identifies its failure from the symptom alone; red = the wrong branch is taken.

The gates consolidation's 'coverage gate unresearched' is wrong: SW-TEST-16 is a watched jq gate over Sources/ lines.
Data.write(.atomic) does not preserve the file mode on Linux 6.3.3/6.4.0 (SW-IO-09, swift-io.md C8).
FileManager.replaceItemAt destroys the new content on Linux 6.3.3; the toolchain's corelibs decide this, not the manifest tools version (SW-IO-09, C11).
The dump-package key is swiftLanguageVersions; the map's M-L-01 jq is wrong (swift-package.md).
LIBDISPATCH_COOPERATIVE_POOL_STRICT is a no-op on Linux, and DispatchQueue.global() is width-limited there (swift-concurrency.md conflicts 4, 9).
Locale.current is en_001 on Linux regardless of LANG, so the premise of M-G-15 is refuted (swift-io.md C7).
NIOFS is not a product to depend on; the module is _NIOFileSystem (SW-PKG underscored-product rule).
The swift:6.4 research image is Ubuntu resolute, so swift-syntax prebuilts were inactive in every wave-2 measurement.
'originHash re-resolves silently' (map, SW-GATE-03 rationale) is overstated; SW-PKG-26/28/29 hold the measured behaviour.
Nuke is a Swift-Testing-only tree, not a mixed one (swift-testing.md).
'No exemplar reads NO_COLOR' is wrong: 7 read sites in 5 repos, 6 of them wrong (swift-cli.md).
A throw out of top-level code exits 132 with a backtrace, not 1 (SW-CLI-02).
Promoting ExplicitSendable to an error behaves differently through SwiftPM (I-V18, exit 0) and swiftc (WC R20, exit 1); only the swiftc form is verified.
contradictions_across_consolidations: 1. SW-CONC-04 ('ExplicitSendable never a gate') vs SW-GATE-17 (promote via -Werror ExplicitSendable or .treatWarning). SW-GATE-17 keeps its text for the -Xswiftc -Werror -Xswiftc ExplicitSendable form only (swiftc-verified); the .treatWarning alternative is struck until measured. SW-CONC-04 keeps the annotation rule and log audit, and its 'never a gate' clause becomes a pointer. Measured in gates/lint-carriers-and-sanitizers.

2. SW-CONC-03 (name NoUseUnstructuredThrowingTask on 6.4 legs) vs SW-GATE-15/C3 (name only groups on the oldest leg). SW-GATE-15 keeps its text: the blanket flag already fails the plant on 6.4 (GC2). SW-CONC-03 keeps its ID and its coverage text, drops its own command, and points to SW-GATE-13 and SW-CONC-13.

3. SW-CONC-21, swift-errors.md C8, swift-io.md C4/verdict 9 and swift-cli.md's SwiftLint conflict ('custom_rules cannot carry bans on Linux') vs SW-GATE-11 and the orchestrator finding. The SW-GATE-10 greps stay the gate and SW-GATE-11 keeps its text. SW-CONC-21's clause is reworded to 'the static binary skips custom_rules silently; use the SourceKit image'. Advisory vs gate is decided next wave.

4. SW-CONC-12 (InferIsolatedConformances only for global-actor modules) vs SW-PKG-08 (enable it in all new packages). SW-PKG-08 keeps the manifest text (the no-op is reasoned, and is confirmed in language/era-and-idioms). SW-CONC-12 keeps NNBD, @concurrent and the template clauses.

5. Duplicate ownership. defaultIsolation: SW-CONC-11 keeps the text and SW-PKG-19 is the manifest pointer. ApproachableConcurrency: SW-PKG-16 keeps the text. StrictLanguageFeatures: SW-PKG-02 has the manifest form and SW-GATE-16 the CI form. unsafeFlags: SW-PKG-04 and SW-GATE-14 agree.
6. SW-GATE-03's rationale (originHash re-resolves silently) vs SW-PKG-26/28/29. SW-PKG keeps the lock policy and rationale; SW-GATE-03 keeps only the CI wiring and cites SW-PKG-28.
7. SW-GATE-10 E08 sleep grep vs SW-TEST-03. SW-TEST-03 keeps its text and its grep replaces E08 verbatim (E08 caught 4 of 7, SW-TEST-03 7 of 7).

8. SW-GATE-10 E16 ([^.A-Za-z_]exit() vs SW-CLI-03. E16 misses Glibc./Darwin./Foundation.exit, _exit and a call at column 1. SW-CLI-03 keeps its text and its first grep replaces E16, keeping E16's --exclude-dir operands.

9. Task.sleep(nanoseconds has three owners: E07, SW-IO-16 and the SW-CONC failure mode 16. SW-IO-16 keeps the rule and E07 stays the gate invocation. Likewise E11 vs SW-IO-05: SW-IO-05 keeps the rule and E11's wider grep is the gate.
10. SW-GATE-10 E14 (NSLock etc.) vs swift-concurrency.md conflict 10. Consistent: E14 is a review prompt, not a ban. SW-CONC keeps the policy (removal test plus guard check).
11. SW-GATE-01 step 3 vs SW-TEST-10 (the XCTest interop env prefix on 6.4+ legs with tools <6.4). SW-TEST-10 keeps the text; the gate block shows the prefix.
12. SW-ERR-05's check (-r Sources --configuration) vs SW-GATE-02's file list. SW-GATE-02 keeps the invocation (C10); SW-ERR-05 keeps the rule and the Never* config.
13. SW-ERR-04 (-Werror UntypedThrows, 6.4-only) vs SW-GATE-15. SW-GATE-15 keeps its text; SW-ERR-04 applies only where the oldest leg is >=6.4, or via @diagnose in one module.
14. SW-ERR-03 (never list FullTypedThrows) vs SW-PKG-02 (the StrictLanguageFeatures guard). Both stay; SW-ERR-03 keeps its reason and cites SW-PKG-02 as its check.

15. SW-PKG-02 (unconditional manifest .treatWarning StrictLanguageFeatures in libraries) vs SW-GATE-14 (library manifest warning control only behind an env switch) and conc owner default 4. SW-PKG-02 keeps its text as a named exception (root-only, consumer exit 0, fires only on unknown names), and SW-GATE-14 gains 'except StrictLanguageFeatures'. Re-measured in gates/lint-carriers-and-sanitizers.

16. Exit tests: SW-ERR-19, SW-TEST-11 and SW-CLI-14. SW-TEST-11 keeps the mechanism, SW-CLI-14 the per-Status contract, and SW-ERR-19 'every documented trap and throw is tested'. swift-testing.md's 'SW-CLI-17' means SW-CLI-14.
17. SW-ERR-17 (64/65/132) vs SW-CLI-01/12. SW-CLI keeps the table and the platform caveat; SW-ERR-17 keeps throw-not-trap and cites SW-CLI-01.

18. SW-CONC-27 vs SW-TEST-17 (TSan). SW-TEST-17 keeps the CI recipe; SW-CONC-27 keeps the count-assertion clause. swift-testing.md's 'SW-CONC-16' means SW-CONC-27. Both are revised if a suppression works.
19. SW-TEST-15 vs SW-IO-25 (pipe draining). SW-IO-25 keeps the pipe rule and SW-TEST-15 the three-facts harness. swift-testing.md's 'SW-IO-P12' means SW-IO-25.
20. The gates open question 'coverage gate unresearched' vs SW-TEST-16. SW-TEST-16 answers it; SW-GATE has no coverage row.

21. SW-IO-26/Q-IO-3 (CancellationError on cancel, timedOut wins) vs SW-CONC-24 (TimeoutError, never CancellationError). Consistent, overlap only: SW-CONC-24 is general and SW-IO-26 is the SDK specialisation. api/sdk-shape pins the precedence.
22. SW-CLI-13 vs SW-IO-05. Consistent: SW-IO-05 keeps the spawn rule and SW-CLI-13 the SIGPIPE-disposition reason.

23. SW-CLI-07 (@preconcurrency import Glibc first) vs SW-IO-04/R3 (Essentials needs a libc import for exit). Consistent; the ordering under FoundationEssentials is measured in cli/services-and-config.
24. SW-CLI-03's fatalError tell vs SW-ERR trap policy. Consistent: SW-ERR owns traps.
25. SW-IO-06 (swift-subprocess from: 1.0.1) vs the SW-PKG pin policy and swift-testing.md's 'harness uses the product's own pin'. Consistent: SW-IO-06 keeps the subprocess pin text.
